Trickster

Overview

Trickster is a resourceful resident of the Ingos settlement. He reasons that the newcomers’ return speaks against the accusations of theft and supports them in front of Geraldine. Later he sends Kir and Kel on a diversion while he obtains the key needed for their onward journey. [1, 2]

The Beastmasters and the empty caravan

At the Beastmasters’ settlement, Crooked accuses Kir and Kel of being spies. Geraldine agrees to test them. Their attempt to obtain a gold nugget from a caravan finds an empty chest, making their return dangerous. Trickster reasons that genuine thieves would not come back empty-handed, and Geraldine accepts them. Sver’s advice about an ice elemental in the abandoned mines provides something to offer Yam-Akara. His work and the governor’s permit requirements then draw the travellers into further dealings with the court. The missing nugget will matter again when the apparent caravan failure becomes evidence of a separate theft. [3, 1, 4, 5, 6]

Brissen’s murder and the failed alibi

Brissen is murdered and Yam-Akara is accused of killing his old friend. Kir and Kel undertake the defence. The magician says he spent the day in the mines and arrived late for their meeting. Mine guard confirms that he allowed the elderly visitor through with an expired permit and stamped it that day. Kir finds the lost pass, but Valrasian rejects the water-damaged document because the signature and date can no longer be read. This evidence supports the search but does not free Yam-Akara; the travellers still have to identify the murderer. [7, 8, 9, 10, 11]

The hidden portal to Jigran

During his confinement, Yam-Akara gains access to the governor’s library. Old exploration reports reveal that the powerful “artifact” is a forgotten passage to another land. Trickster offers a key to the gate, then sends Kir on a fruitless ore search so that he can work without interference. With the key ready, Yam-Akara warns that he cannot sense the destination: the portal may be defective or concealed by a powerful absorbing spell. Kir recognises the same absence Tka-Rik described and concludes that it leads to Jigran. He decides to go directly, trusting the strength gained during his journey. Kel chooses to accompany him again. [12, 13, 2, 14]
